about: Ring-out time measured on given audio — ringOutTime(samples, from: start, to: end, sampleRate:, threshold:) — the same cases in every edition. Each case's audio is generated from 'signal': 'length' samples at 'sampleRate', silent before 'onset', then amplitude·exp(−n/(timeConstant·sampleRate)) (amplitude 0.5 unless given), scaled up linearly over the first 'attack' samples when given, stored as 32-bit floats. 'threshold' is the decay threshold in dB when given (else 'defaultThreshold', the analyzer's default); 'expect' is seconds, or null for no ring-out, within 'tolerance'. The level is the energy of every 'windowSamples'-sample window. 'analyzer' holds cases on the analyzer itself, as steps on a fresh analyzer: {"decayTime": s} sets the ring-out shown; {"newTap": true} starts a new tap sequence. 'expect' is 'currentDecayTime' after the last step (null for none).

ringOutTime.note: an exponential decay from the onset: its level falls in a straight line in dB, so the crossing is exact — 15 dB below the peak at 0.75·ln10·τ
the same decay with a 20 dB threshold: 1·ln10·τ
silence before the onset, measured from before it: the windows that reach into the silence hold less energy, so the peak and the crossing are those of DK1
an attack — the level rises for 10 ms before it decays: the peak is after the onset, and the ring-out is measured from it
a decay too slow to fall 15 dB before the end: no ring-out
no more audio than one window: no ring-out
the end is where the audio is cut: a decay that crosses after it measures nothing

analyzer.note: a new sequence clears the last ring-out
